ja: הד'א אלמעני אם רוח המושל תעלה עליך מקומך אל תנח. ואלכ'אמסה, ענד תקריעה ואכ'ד' אלקצאץ ללה מנה. ואנתצאף ד'וי אלחקוק מן מאלה, פאן תברא בהא לאצחאבהא טועא וסארע אלי אכ'ד' אלקצאץ ללה מנה מע תעד'ר ד'לך עלי אלחכם מנה, צח תואצ'עה ללה וכ'שועה ואנכ'פאצ'ה, כקול עזרא ע"ס אנחנו מעלנו באלהינו ונשב נשים נכריות, וקאל ויתנו ידם להוציא נשיהם. וענד הד'ה אלחואדת' ושבההא תבדו אעלאם אלתואצ'ע ואלכ'שוע מן אלמתואצ'עין, ויט'הר צדק צ'מירהם ללה פיהא. פצל. ח. קאל, ואמא הל אלתואצ'ע תאל ללפצ'איל, אם אלפצ'איל תאליה לה. פאקול פי אלג'ואב ען ד'לך, אן אלמעלום ענדנא, אן אוול טאעהֵ אללה עז וג'ל מן אלאנסאן פהו אלתברי אליה בצפאת אלרבוביה ואפראדה בהא, ואלתזאמה ג'מיע צפאת אלעבודיה ללה, ואלעבודיה ואלרבוביה פמן באב אלמצ'אף אלד'י ילזם וג'וד אחדהמא בוג'וד אלאכ'ר, פאן אלאנסאן לא יסתחק אסם עבד חתי יכון לה רב, ואלרב לא יסתחק הד'א אלאסם חתי יכון לה עבד, אד' המא פי מעני אלמאלך ואלממלוך אלד'אן לא יסבק אחדהמא צאחבה באלנסבה ואלתסמיה. פלא תצח מן אלאנסאן אלטאעה ללה אלא באלזאם נפסה ג'מיע צפאת אלעבודיה לה, והי אלתואצ'ע

**The third**: when his report spreads among people, in good or in evil. If a praiser praises him for a good deed he has done, he undermines his praiser in it; he despises it within himself; he counts it small in his eye, that God should accept it from him and be satisfied with him by it, on account of its smallness in the face of what is binding upon him of the like of that good deed. He says to his praiser: "Cut short, my brother — for it is, in the face of my sins, only as the spark of fire in the sea; and even if it had measure, how could I attain its salvation from the misfortunes of corruption that attach to it, that my Lord receive it from me, and not turn it back upon me, and not throw it in my face — as He said: 'When you come to see My face, who has sought this from your hand, to trample My courts?' (Isaiah 1:12); and: 'Bring no more vain offerings; the smoke of incense is an abomination to Me' (Isaiah 1:13)." How much more so if it was vain — it is incumbent upon him to aim at negating it from himself, and to say to the one who described him by it: "Enough, my brother, of my falling-short in what is binding upon me toward God; do not gather upon me the sin of falling-short *and* the sin of self-adornment by what I have not done; for I am more knowledgeable than you of what I bear within of sins and heedlessnesses" — as he said: "For I know my transgressions, and my sin is ever before me" (Psalms 51:5).

If he is mentioned for a bad deed he has done, he confesses against himself his falling-short in it; he aims neither at excuse nor at self-adornment in it — as Judah (peace be upon him) said: "She is more righteous than I" (Genesis 38:26). Let him not make the describer fall short, nor accuse him of lying about it. Let him not ascribe blame to him for the uncovering of it, but say to him: "My brother, what is the measure of what you have come to know of the badness of my work, in the face of what you have not known of it — concerning which God's covering of me has long endured? If the badness of my deeds and my sins were to dawn upon you, you would flee from me out of fear of God's punishment for them" — as one of the poets said: *"Were my neighbors to smell out my sins, they would flee and depart from my borders."* Job (peace be upon him) said: "If I have hidden my transgression like Adam, by concealing my iniquity in my bosom…" (Job 31:33).

If what he was ascribed of is false, let him say to the one who described him by it: "My brother, it is not from wonder, God's preserving me from the doing of what you have ascribed to me, in the face of His abundant bounty toward me. The wonder is, rather, God's covering upon me of what is more ugly and more shocking by far than what you have described me by. So cut short, my brother, and have pity on your good deeds, that they not depart from you while you do not perceive."

It has been said of one of the people of bounty: he was mentioned ill, and the report came to him; he sent to the one who slandered him a tray of the rare delicacies of his town and wrote to him: "It has reached me, my brother, that you have presented me with some of your good deeds; I saw fit to recompense you with this." One of the righteous said: "Many people may come on the Day of the Reckoning, and when their deeds are presented to them, they shall find in the registry of their good deeds good deeds they did not do, and they shall deny them; it shall be said to them: 'They were done by those who slandered you and took from your reputation.' Likewise when the good deeds of the slanderers fall, they shall seek them at that point; it shall be said to them: 'They fell from you when you slandered so-and-so and so-and-so.' So too some of them shall find in the registry of their bad deeds bad deeds they did not do, and when they deny them they shall be told: 'You caused them to fall from so-and-so and so-and-so by your slander and ill-speech of them, and you have deserved them from them, since their good deeds were insufficient against them' — as He said: 'Return to our neighbors sevenfold into their bosom the reproach with which they have reproached You, O Lord' (Psalms 79:12)." From this concept Scripture has warned us, in His saying: "Remember what the Lord your God did to Miriam by the way" (Deuteronomy 24:9).
